introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Economics 2 (0525), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2025. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Instructions to candidates: You are required to answer ANY FIVE questions. ONLY THE FIRST FIVE QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED. All the questions carry equal marks. Calculators are allowed.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following:

(i) Mode. (2 marks)
(ii) Scarcity. (2 marks)
(iii) Utility. (2 marks)
(iv) Consumer sovereignty. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Mode.** The mode is the **value that occurs most frequently** in a set of data (the most common item). Example: in the shoe sizes 38, 39, 39, 40, 39, 41 the mode is 39. A set of data can have more than one mode.

**(ii) Scarcity.** Scarcity is the **limited supply of resources (land, labour, capital, enterprise) in relation to the unlimited wants of human beings**. Because resources are scarce, people, firms and governments must make choices and give up some wants to satisfy others. It is the basic economic problem.

**(iii) Utility.** Utility is the **satisfaction (want-satisfying power) that a consumer obtains from consuming a good or service**. A good has utility if it can satisfy a want, whether or not it is useful in a moral sense.

**(iv) Consumer sovereignty.** Consumer sovereignty is the situation in which **consumers, by their spending decisions, decide what is produced**: producers make the goods that consumers are willing to buy at a profit, and stop making those that nobody buys. Consumers are "kings" of the market.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) State and explain THREE (3) advantages of a market economy. (6 marks)

(ii) State and explain THREE (3) characteristics of a public good. (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Three advantages of a market economy.** A market economy is one in which resources are allocated by the price mechanism (demand and supply) with private ownership and little state intervention.

1. **Efficient allocation of resources.** Prices act as signals: when demand for a good rises, its price and profit rise, so resources move into producing it, and out of goods that nobody wants. No central planner is needed to decide what to produce.
2. **Consumer sovereignty, choice and variety.** Firms compete to satisfy consumers, so there is a wide choice of goods and services, and what is produced follows what consumers want to buy.
3. **Incentives for efficiency, enterprise and innovation.** The profit motive and competition push firms to cut costs, improve quality and invent new products, and reward hard-working and risk-taking people; this raises output and living standards.

**(ii) Three characteristics of a public good.** A public good (for example street lighting, national defence, police protection) has the following features.

1. **Non-excludable.** Once it is provided, nobody can be prevented from using it, even if the person does not pay, so a price cannot be charged to each user. This leads to the *free-rider* problem, and private firms are unwilling to supply it.
2. **Non-rival (non-rivalrous) in consumption.** One person's use does not reduce the amount available to others: the same street light or army protects everybody, and an extra user adds no extra cost.
3. **Provided by the government and paid for out of taxation.** Since it cannot be sold in the market, it is financed collectively by taxes and supplied by the state (or by a body it appoints), and the quantity is decided collectively rather than by individual buyers.
